Paragraph: Summary of Passage: By becoming free from attachment, fear, and anger, and by absorbing themselves in divine devotion, many seekers have been purified through knowledge and attained divine love.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Overcoming emotional toxins—attachment, fear, and anger—to achieve inner purity and love.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna outlines the path of purification: 'vita-raga-bhaya-krodha man-maya mam upasritah, bahavo jnana-tapasa puta mad-bhavam agatah' (Freed from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me, purified by wisdom and austerity, many have attained My nature).
Outcome/Resolution: Provides a tested spiritual method for emotional purification and attaining divine love.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Freedom from Emotional Toxins: Overcoming reactivity driven by attachment, fear, and resentment
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Mindful Absorption: Focusing attention fully on positive, stabilizing anchors
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Purification and Growth: Cleansing the mind through self-discipline and self-knowledge

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Vita-raga-bhaya-krodha (Freed from attachment, fear, and anger)
Man-maya mam upasritah (Absorbed in the Divine and taking refuge in Him)
Jnana-tapasa puta (Purified by the fire of knowledge and self-discipline)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Releasing attachment, fear, and anger while taking refuge in the Divine purifies the seeker through spiritual wisdom, elevating them to transcendental love.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Releasing emotional baggage—such as obsession, anxiety, and resentment—clears the mind, enabling deeper peace and healthier relationships.
